changes: A gateway middleware instead of a local HTTP proxy: no port, no base_url change, and one file with no imports.
PerProvider: it acts in onProvider on the provider ids the options name, so a group, a fallback or a direct request is changed only on the tries that reach one of them.

What it removes is a superset of the proxy's: item ids, every encrypted* field (not only top level ones), a content part of type encrypted_content, and item_reference, which holds nothing but an id on the resource.

Ids are stripped from content-bearing items and retained native reasoning. true and omission use the same whitelist; ids: "all" includes unknown item types. Compaction checkpoints always bypass stripping. The original content-bearing whitelist came from codex-history (MIT, itself from Codex Filter Manager).

include is never touched: it asks for reasoning in the reply, not for the history's ciphertext, and an upstream may turn the request away over a changed include (codex-history's note, kept here and covered by a case).

historySearch: "note" uses codex-history's v0.1.1 web_search_call conversion. In 0.1.1 it defaults on when encrypted reasoning is removed, so a past native search no longer depends on a removed reasoning item. Explicit keep preserves native calls; encrypted:false defaults to keep.

store: false is sent by default, as the proxy does not need to but magpie does: a provider magpie takes for Azure or OpenAI keeps responses itself and would otherwise send the next turn as the new input alone under its own id (internal/gateway/prev_response.go, prevKeeps and prevDelta).

previous_response_id is removed only with previousResponse: "drop". The proxy removes it always; in magpie the field has already been resolved and deleted when magpie holds the response, so one still present is a response magpie does not hold, and removing it can drop the history a client that sends only its new turn relies on.

In 0.1.1 native compaction items are preserved whole and produce recovery guidance rather than losing earlier context. The plugin cannot decrypt a checkpoint or recover history absent from the request.

In 0.1.1 encryption cleanup removes reasoning items whole, turning their readable summary/content into ordinary history notes rather than leaving empty reasoning shells. This matches the effective operation of the earlier local Codex session repair.

The repository includes an independently authored Magpie integration patch against 60f0433d1b1d500a9939eced3dfe6c54232051af. It reuses the existing JS middleware chain for agent-requested text compaction without recording synthetic summary turns or reentering asynchronous gateway hooks.
Chat and Messages requests are left alone: only a Responses request carries Azure resource state.

Request fields are processed in memory. Readable reasoning and search records become text notes; no history or credential files are read or written. Logs contain counts and compaction recovery guidance, not request content.
